what_it_does: High-performance computing (HPC) uses specialized instruction sets like RISC-V (a free, open processor architecture). This work adds vector processing extensions to RISC-V to efficiently handle multi-word arithmetic—operations on numbers larger than the processor's native word size. Multi-word arithmetic is essential for cryptography and number theory in HPC. The paper models performance across different processor designs and demonstrates the extension on post-quantum cryptography kernels.
